'''Pantur Silaban''' (11 November 1937 – 1 August 2022) was an Indonesian physicist, regarded as one of the foremost in his profession in Indonesia, especially in the field of [[theoretical physics]]. He was also one of the earliest physicists from [[ASEAN]] countries who studied [[Albert Einstein|Einstein's]] [[general relativity]] theories in depth.

==Early life ==
Pantur Silaban was born in Sumatra to Israel Silaban and Regina Lumbantoruan in Dairi Regency in [[Sumatra]], Indonesia.

He finished his bachelor's degree in [[physics]] from [[Bandung Institute of Technology]], Indonesia in 1964.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fisikanet.lipi.go.id/utama.cgi?cetakartikel&1365859689|title=Si Jenius Fisika dari Tanah Batak : PANTUR SILABAN – Dari Snellius ke Einstein|author1=Sirait, P. Hasudungan|author2=Naipospos, Nabisuk|language=id|access-date=7 June 2014|archive-date=8 June 2014|archive-url=https://archive.today/20140608010322/http://www.fisikanet.lipi.go.id/utama.cgi?cetakartikel&1365859689|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Career==
In 1967, Silaban went to the United States to study [[General Relativity]] theory at ''Central Studies of Gravitation'' at [[Syracuse University]] under the direction of [[Peter Bergmann]] and [[Joshua N. Goldberg]] who were among the authoritative experts in general relativity after [[Albert Einstein]]. Here, Silaban went further to study one of the hottest topics in physics at the time which tried to unify quantum field and general relativity to find quantum gravity theory. It is one of Einstein's dreams which had tried but failed to formalize the fourth interaction in the universe into one single theory called [[Grand Unified Theory]].

Instead of insisting on working on quantum gravity, Silaban eventually followed the advice of Goldberg to change the subject for his dissertation: to amputate the principle of General Relativity using the Poincare Group to find a physical quantity that is conserved in gravitational radiation. These findings confirmed the [[Big Bang]] as a model for the formation of the Universe rather than the other models.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://fisikanet.lipi.go.id/utama.cgi/utama.cgi?cetakartikel&1365859689|title=Si Jenius Fisika dari Tanah Batak : PANTUR SILABAN – Dari Snellius ke Einstein|author1=Sirait, P. Hasudungan |author2=Naipospos, Nabisuk |language=id|access-date=6 December 2016}}</ref> Silaban finished his dissertation with the title "Null Tetrad, Formulation of the Equation of Motion in General Relativity" in 1971.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fisikanet.lipi.go.id/utama.cgi?cetakartikel&1096193952|title=Lebih jauh dengan Pantur Silaban|language=id|access-date=7 June 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|title=Null Tetrad Formulation of the Equations of Motion in General Relativity|first=Pantur|last=Silaban|publisher=Syracuse University|year=1971|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=g5wamwEACAAJ|bibcode=1971PhDT.......168S}}</ref>

Three years later Joshua Goldberg – who produces many important physics treatises published in major journals such as ''Physical Review D'', ''Journal of Mathematical Physics'', and Journal ''of Geometrical Physics'' – referred to Silaban's work in his paper, ''Conservation Equations and Equations of Motion in the Null Formalism''.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Conservation Equations and Equations of Motion in the Null Formalism|journal=General Relativity and Gravitation|bibcode=1974GReGr...5..183G|first=Joshua N.|last=Goldberg|volume=5|issue=2|pages=183–200|year=1974|doi=10.1007/BF00763500|s2cid=119825205}}</ref>

A year after completing his dissertation, Silaban went back to [[Bandung]] in 1972 and taught at the Department of Physics, [[Bandung Institute of Technology]].  Silaban was the first Indonesian scientist who studied General Relativity to a doctoral level. Besides general relativity, he also studied [[Particle physics]].

Silaban became a [[Professor (highest academic rank)|full professor]] at [[Institut Teknologi Bandung|ITB]] in 1995.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.silaban.net/2008/03/04/pantur-silaban-dari-snellius-ke-einstein/|title=The Pantur Silaban: From Snellius To Einstein|access-date=15 October 2008|publisher=Silaban Brotherhood|language=id|archive-date=15 October 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081015155237/http://www.silaban.net/2008/03/04/pantur-silaban-dari-snellius-ke-einstein/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Less than a month after Bergmann died, Silaban retired from ITB in November 2002 at the age of 65.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fisikanet.lipi.go.id/utama.cgi?artikel&1047747600|title=Cucu Murid Einstein Itu Kini Pensiun|language=id|author=Simanungkalit, Salomo|date=8 March 2003|access-date=19 August 2015|archive-date=12 February 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170212163757/http://www.fisikanet.lipi.go.id/utama.cgi?artikel&1047747600|url-status=dead}}</ref>  For his contribution to science, especially physics, Freedom Institute – Center of Democracy, Nationalism, and Market Economy Studies awarded him the Achmad Bakrie Award in 2009.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://nasional.news.viva.co.id/news/read/83141-murid_einstein_peraih_achmad_bakrie_award|title=Murid Einstein Peraih Achmad Bakrie Award|language=id|author=Siswanto, Mohammad Adam|date=16 August 2009|access-date=19 August 2015}}</ref><!--Place new references above this line-->
